conventions.convention: The tensor rule is left-to-right: lowering selects the first factor when φ_i(b₁)>ε_i(b₂), while raising selects it when φ_i(b₁)≥ε_i(b₂). A zero selected-factor image makes the whole tensor image zero.

Weights are chosen P-grading labels, and tensor labels add. The coproduct is ΔE_i=E_i⊗K_i⁻¹+1⊗E_i and ΔF_i=F_i⊗1+K_i⊗F_i. Integrability alone does not include finite weight spaces or cone-bounded support.

Admissible string coefficients beyond a string's bottom are zero. For a lattice lift of a basis vertex, the unique coefficient surviving modulo q has index ε_i of that vertex; F_i^(−1) is interpreted as zero.
A highest vertex is killed by every raising operator. F(b) consists of nonzero lowering words from b; being highest and generating the entire crystal are separate conditions.

The decomposition theorem assumes AC, finite-dimensional label-weight spaces, and support in a finite union of upper cones λ−Q₊. The constituent family may be infinite but is locally weight-finite. AC supplies semisimple decomposition and simultaneous top-residue lifts.
Duality negates weights, swaps finite ε_i and φ_i, reverses arrows, and reverses tensor-factor order. The proposition excludes the negative-half crystal with its possibly negative formal φ_i.

load_bearing.statement: For integrable chosen P-graded type-one quantum weight modules with crystal bases (L₁,B₁),(L₂,B₂), (L₁⊗_{A₀}L₂,B₁⊗B₂) is a crystal basis of M₁⊗M₂ with the stated strict-lowering/non-strict-raising rule and partial-inverse axiom. No finite dimensionality, bounded support, uniform nilpotence or choice principle is assumed.

Assume AC. A crystal basis (L,B) of an integrable chosen P-graded type-one module with finite-dimensional label-weight spaces and support in finitely many cones λ−Q₊ admits a module isomorphism to a locally weight-finite direct sum of V(λ_j), carrying L to the direct sum of canonical lattices and B bijectively to the disjoint union of canonical crystals. Its connected components are exactly these crystals, with unique dominant highest vertices and constituent multiplicities.

Every admissible i-string coefficient of a homogeneous lattice vector belongs to the lattice. A zero residue has all coefficients in qL; a basis residue has exactly one coefficient outside qL, at index ε_i, whose residue is its raised string top.

The coproduct tensor of chosen P-graded type-one weight modules has the sum grading; integrability is preserved. Finite-dimensional label-weight spaces and finite upper-cone bounds are preserved when both factors have them. The tensor of two crystal lattices is free, generates the tensor module, and has the tensor residue basis.

For crystal bases of integrable modules, wt(b₁⊗b₂)=wt(b₁)+wt(b₂), ε_i(b₁⊗b₂)=max(ε_i(b₁),ε_i(b₂)−⟨h_i,wt(b₁)⟩), and φ_i(b₁⊗b₂)=max(φ_i(b₁)+⟨h_i,wt(b₂)⟩,φ_i(b₂)); the stated branch, tie, partial-inverse and string-iteration properties hold.

For λ∈P⁺, the canonical crystal B(λ) has highest vertex b_λ, equals F(b_λ), and has no other highest vertex. Every nonzero homogeneous residue at a weight other than λ is moved by some raising operator.

alerts.finding: F4 attributes to thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule the additional phrase 'saturated tensor lattice structure on the finite-weight-space category'. The cited theorem establishes tensor crystal-basis axioms and operator rules, but states no saturation property. The consumer does not identify the ambient module or inclusion relative to which this saturation is intended. Its uses of F4 in Step 3.2 need the residue basis, which the supplier does establish.

F3 says 'Every integrable module with finite weight multiplicities and weights bounded above decomposes canonically into a locally weight-finite direct sum of highest weight crystals and their modules'. The cited thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals assumes a given crystal basis and asserts existence of an isomorphism; it determines the crystal graph up to isomorphism, not a canonical module splitting. The actual Fock application supplies a crystal basis and needs only existence, so the issue is the stronger wording of F3.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplying string decomposition, lattice axioms, rank-one tensor rule, graph invariants, canonical lowering lattices and grand-loop theorem against their uses. The general tensor proof uses finite rank-one rectangles rather than category-O or global-integral assumptions. The canonical highest-crystal argument is conditional on the supplied canonical crystal basis.

The actual tensor crystal-lattice and residue-basis uses are supported, and the page keeps globalization separate. However, F4 of thm-quasi-r-tensor-bars-on-finite-products-of-based-integrable-modules adds an unspecified saturation property absent from the cited tensor-rule theorem; reported as an alert.

The finite node-cube tensor rule, empty-component application with finite label spaces and upper-cone support, and diagram-reflection use of canonical lowering words are supported. F3 of thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero overstates the supplier as a canonical module decomposition and omits its given-crystal-basis premise; reported as an alert.
